meta.question: what is Benefit Charges, please? Can I protest Benefit Charges as well?

question: what is Benefit Charges, please? Can I protest Benefit Charges as well?

answers: Benefit charges refer to the UI benefits paid to an unemployed claimant that can impact your UI rate. These charges are spread among all of the claimant’s employers over the 12-month period that establishes their claim. Yes, you can protest benefit charges. To protest benefit charges online, you can log in to e-Services for Business, select 'Show More' from the Account Management panel, choose 'Protest Benefit Charges', enter the required information, and submit. After you submit this information, you will receive a confirmation number. If you prefer to protest by mail, you can use the DE 428T Protest Sample Form (DE 428C) or create your own document, and mail your written protest to: Employment Development Department Contribution Rate Group, MIC 4 PO Box 826831 Sacramento, CA 94230-6831.

history.content: What is the percentage of UI rate assigned to New Employers and how do we get UI rates?

New employers are assigned a 3.4 percent UI rate for two to three years. To get your UI rate, you can visit Get My UI Rate, enter your employer payroll tax account number, and select Get My UI Rate. Also, payroll agents can get UI rates for multiple clients by logging into e-Services for Business and selecting More and then Submit a Bulk Rate Inquiry from the Other Actions Section. If you acquired a business with employees, you have the option of keeping the previous owner's UI tax rate.
I do not agree with my UI rate, I want to protest my UI rate, please.

You can protest your UI rates from the DE 2088 or benefit charges on the DE 428T online or by mail. To protest your UI rate online, you can follow these steps:
1. Log in to e-Services for Business.
2. Select 'Show More' from the Account Management panel.
3. Select 'Protest UI Rate'.
4. Enter the required information and submit.
After you submit this information, you will receive a confirmation number. 
If you prefer to protest by mail, you can include your EDD employer payroll tax account number, the items you want to protest, the reason for protesting, and mail your written protest to: Employment Development DepartmentRate Management Group, MIC 4PO Box 826880Sacramento, CA 94280-0001. Please note that protests with missing or incorrect information will be returned.

Protest Benefit Charges by Mail 

You can use the DE 428T Protest Sample Form (DE 428C) (PDF) or create your own document. You must include:

Your EDD employer payroll tax account number.
Each claimant’s name and Social Security number.
Each claim date.
Charge amount.
The specific reason for protesting the charges.
Total number of claimants being protested.

Protests with missing or incorrect information will be returned. Mail your written protest or request for an extension to:
